context_label_definitions.child_ownership: The sensitive information in the message belongs to, or describes, the person typing. 'My number is ...' is true; 'my mom's number is ...' is false. A message with no sensitive information at all is false.
context_label_definitions.child_location: A location in the message is where the person typing is, lives, or will be. 'I live at 24 Oak Street' is true; 'the restaurant is at 24 Oak Street' is false. Past locations they are no longer at are false.
context_label_definitions.school_context: The message reveals which school the person attends, or where/when they are at it. Naming a school someone else attends, or a school as a landmark, is false.
context_label_definitions.routine: The message describes repeated, predictable behaviour by the person typing — something an outsider could use to know where they will be in future. Requires a recurrence cue ('every Tuesday', 'always', 'after school'), not a one-off plan.
context_label_definitions.specific_time: The message pins an event to a time precise enough to act on — a clock time, a named part of a specific day, or a countdown. 'Later' and 'sometime' are false.
context_label_definitions.alone: The message indicates the person typing is, or will be, physically unaccompanied. 'Leave me alone' and the film 'Home Alone' are false.
context_label_definitions.guardian_absent: The message indicates a parent, guardian, or other supervising adult is away or will be. Distinct from `alone`: a sibling may be home. Both are often true.
context_label_definitions.meetup: The message proposes, arranges, or agrees to an in-person meeting — including inviting someone to a location. Reporting a meeting that already happened is false.
